name: HOTAS BF6 Simple
tagline: A fast, low-latency Windows HOTAS mapper built around Battlefield 6 and vJoy.
summary: HOTAS BF6 Simple maps a selected physical DirectInput controller into the virtual controls Battlefield 6 can reliably bind through vJoy. v2.0.0 introduced persistent universal DirectInput device management; v2.0.2 completes its dashboard, settings, tray, and controller-switching polish while preserving the high-performance mapping engine. The product combines deterministic real-time input processing with persistent controller memory, profiles, advanced response curves, button and POV routing, Automation, diagnostics, three themes, a native installer/updater, and HOTAS Setup & Verification.
purpose: The project exists to make HOTAS input practical in Battlefield 6 without placing UI work, network work, allocation-heavy logic, or persistence on the mapper hot path.

principles.name: Mapper-first performance
principles.description: Input processing and vJoy output are isolated from the QML UI. Configuration is compiled outside the report loop and swapped in between reports.

principles.name: Deterministic behavior
principles.description: Profiles, automation, button controls, POV routing, and axis transforms use explicit precedence and bounded runtime state rather than timing-sensitive UI logic.

principles.name: Safe output states
principles.description: Mapping Off, controller loss, disabled routes, and unsupported virtual outputs resolve to deliberate parked or centered states instead of leaving stale commands active.

principles.name: Configuration without hot-path cost
principles.description: Rich editing, live graphs, readable automation summaries, and themes operate in presentation/configuration layers and do not add per-report UI work.

principles.name: Capability-aware hardware integration
principles.description: HOTAS Setup & Verification combines passive startup checks with a user-requested full device check, uses mapper-owned evidence when available, and keeps all driver work outside the mapping worker.

principles.name: Conservative dependency handling
principles.description: Installed dependencies are inspected first. Any automatic vJoy/HidHide repair is previewed, explicitly approved, minimally scoped, verified, and rolled back when a transaction fails.

signalPath: Axis inversion and response curve lookup
Profile-owned output limits and axis domain
Safe routing to available vJoy axes, buttons, and POVs
Battlefield 6 binding to the virtual vJoy device
usage: Install the latest HOTAS BF6 setup package from GitHub Releases.
Open HOTAS BF6 at Overview. Choose a connected controller in Settings when more than one is available; a new controller opens themed setup after selection.
Open Settings and choose VERIFY HOTAS SETUP to deeply verify the selected physical controller, vJoy Device 1, and HidHide configuration.

Review any exact proposed repair, then choose FIX AUTOMATICALLY only if it matches your intent. HOTAS BF6 executes required vJoy/HidHide changes through one approved elevated transaction and restores the Mapping On/Off state that preceded the repair.
Confirm READY, then select or create a profile.
Configure axis routes, domains, output limits, curves, button routes, POV behavior, and game-facing labels.
Use Mapping On/Off controls and Diagnostics to confirm neutral behavior before binding controls in Battlefield 6.
Add Automation only after the base mapping is behaving correctly; new rules begin as disabled drafts and must validate before they can run.

troubleshooting.symptom: HOTAS Setup & Verification cannot find vJoyConfig or HidHideCLI
troubleshooting.guidance: Use the official dependency installer or complete the configuration manually. HOTAS BF6 will not download, update, or silently change an already-installed driver.

troubleshooting.symptom: vJoy Device 1 is busy, disabled, or lacks required outputs
troubleshooting.guidance: When HOTAS BF6 already owns Device 1 while mapping, that is Ready. If another application owns it, close that application, then verify again. Automatic repair refuses to overwrite a busy target.

troubleshooting.symptom: A game sees both the physical controller and vJoy
troubleshooting.guidance: Review the selected physical controller and HidHide findings in HOTAS Setup & Verification. Only hide the exact selected HID instance after confirming the mapper is allowlisted; leave unrelated devices untouched.

troubleshooting.symptom: Mapping or game binding is still not behaving as expected
troubleshooting.guidance: Use Mapping Off to neutralize output, inspect Diagnostics and HOTAS Setup & Verification, then report the application version, Windows version, selected controller, vJoy summary, HidHide state, and reproducible steps.

compatibility.official: Battlefield 6 uses EA Javelin anticheat. HOTAS BF6 does not claim EA endorsement, official approval, or guaranteed anticheat compatibility.
compatibility.utility: HOTAS BF6 is an accessibility-style input-mapping utility: it reads a selected physical DirectInput controller and writes a vJoy virtual controller. It is not intended to create an unfair competitive advantage.
compatibility.verified: Repository evidence verifies deterministic mapper behavior, headless tests, packaging gates, and the HOTAS Setup & Verification planner/transaction logic. It does not by itself verify a live Battlefield session, anticheat acceptance, a particular physical controller, installer interaction, UAC behavior on a particular machine, or updater interaction.
compatibility.windows: Azure Artifact Signing with GitHub OIDC is prepared for trusted stable releases, but its Public Trust certificate profile is pending Microsoft identity validation. Until that profile exists, manual release runs are explicitly unsigned dry runs and stable tag publication is blocked. Local self-signing is development-only and never a public-release identity.
compatibility.reporting: Report regressions with application version, Windows version, selected controller name and exact HOTAS Setup & Verification findings, vJoy capability summary, HidHide state, and steps to reproduce. Do not attach unrelated device lists or sensitive system data.
